newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Norwegian savings banks bid for Fokus Bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Norwegian savings banks bid for Fokus Bank.

text.p: Sixteen savings banks made a hostile takeover bid on Monday for Norway's fourth largest bank, Fokus Bank, in the latest attempt at consolidation in the country's overbanked financial sector.
Sparebankgruppen said it was bidding 73 crowns per share for Fokus, which it valued at 4.80 billion ($690 million). The group said it controlled, directly or indirectly, 10 percent of Fokus.
Shares in Fokus, which is 80 percent owned by foreign investors, were up eight percent to 74 crowns in afternoon trade on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
Analysts said the price was attractive for shareholders but Fokus Bank managing director Bjarne Borgersen criticised Sparebankgruppen.
"I see it as a hostile takeover bid because this is not something we have had a chance to discuss," Borgersen told Reuters.
"We are sceptical both of the bid and their plans for Fokus. For the moment I have no opinion on the price but I am not convinced it is the right price," he said.
Fokus, which specialises in regional banking, posted 1996 net profits of 462 million crowns, up 7.7 percent on 1995.
Sparebankgruppen, which consists of small regional savings banks, said it planned to integrate the business of Fokus with the respective regional savings banks.
Fokus, which is the fruit of fusions between seven banks between 1987 and 1991, would thus cease to exist.
The statement said a takeover of Fokus would produce a significant regional consolidation in Norway's financial sector.
"It is a natural development for Fokus to disappear," an Oslo-based analyst said. "There is overcapacity in the market and this is a way to reduce it."
Sparebankgruppen is owned by Sparebanken Nord-Norge, Sparebanken Midt-Norge, Sparebanken Vest, Sparebanken Rogaland and 12 other, unlisted savings banks.
The group said a takeover was conditional on Fokus not acquiring niche mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) but Borgersen said Fokus had not given up its attempt to take over BNbank.

"We feel that a merger with BNbank would increase the wealth of our shareholders," he said. "Sparebankgruppen is coming with their bid now in order to stop us from merging with BNbank because such a merger would make us too big and expensive for them."
Fokus is locked in a battle for BNbank with Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's biggest bank. The mortgage lender last week inclined towards accepting DnB's bid but no decision has yet been made.
DnB spokesman Jarl Veggan said DnB had no plans to outbid the savings banks for Fokus but he said: "This is another confirmation that the restructuring in the Norwegian bank sector is not over."
Earlier this month merger plans were announced by Norway's second largest bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, and the country's largest insurer, Storebrand.

The merger, if approved by shareholders and authorities, would form the country's largest financial group -- larger than DnB -- and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region. ($ = 6.960 Norwegian Crowns)
